EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours is the declared cancellation of an impending US attack on Iran by President Trump, citing an agreement framework on the immediate opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. However, this claim is directly contradicted by Iranian officials, who deny any such agreement regarding Hormuz and state the strategic waterway remains closed. This profound divergence in narratives creates significant uncertainty and maintains high regional tensions.

IRAN
US President Trump announced he cancelled a planned attack on Iran at the request of Iran and other Middle Eastern countries, claiming an agreement framework had been reached for the immediate, complete, and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. This claim was swiftly and vehemently denied by Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei and Fars News Agency, who called it "fake news" and stated that no agreement on reopening Hormuz exists, emphasizing that the strait remains closed as long as US hostile actions continue. Military sources cited by Fars maintained that passage through Hormuz requires explicit authorization from the IRGC Navy.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that negotiations with Oman regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz are in their "final stages," though Spokesperson Baghaei clarified these talks do not pertain to opening or closing the strait, asserting Iran's future management of Hormuz. Contrarily, Channel 12 Israel reported Araghchi agreed to a Qatari-US compromise for reopening Hormuz, which allegedly led Trump to call off strikes, with Oman seeking IRGC confirmation for the deal.

Internally, President Pezeshkian endorsed a memorandum between Tehran and Washington as a "collective wisdom of the members of SNSC," believing it will be the cornerstone of future foreign relations and enhance regional security. Acting Defense Minister Brigadier General Seyyed Majid Ibn Al-Reza affirmed that Iran's armed forces are prepared for threats and will not be caught by surprise. An Iranian diplomat reportedly indicated to the Wall Street Journal that the IRGC is considering pre-emptive strikes if diplomatic efforts fail, even without a US attack.

Economically, Iran faces challenges including a reduction in the second gasoline quota (from 70 to 50 liters per month) and a soaring US dollar price nearing 196,000 Tomans. Inflation is evident with reported price increases for chicken and meat (200%), milk (150%), yogurt and cheese (136%), liquid oil (350%), solid oil (415%), and fruits (110%). Over 180 fast-food businesses in Shiraz closed in two months due to reduced purchasing power. Iran claimed localization of 2,000 sanctioned petrochemical components.

In security incidents, one soldier named Abulfazl Goodarzi was killed and another injured in an attack by PJAK using two suicide drones and RPGs on a military headquarters in Maryvan. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated receiving calls from the UK, Bulgaria, and Ukraine affirming they would not be part of a war against Iran. Iran also warned Saudi Arabia of a "powerful" response if US or Israeli attacks occur, especially if Gulf states participate. Reports indicate an Iranian commercial ship suffered an alleged Ukrainian attack, resulting in one sailor's death. The New York Post claimed protest leaders in Iran are arming, suggesting a revolution could occur "any moment."

ISRAEL
Defense Minister Israel Katz's attempt to replace IDF Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth was met with strong condemnation and non-cooperation from the IDF. The military stated Katz's announcement was "not coordinated" with Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, who has "no intention of replacing commanders in key positions during this sensitive period." Katz publicly denounced Bluth over a restraining order against a settler, stating he seeks commanders with a "proven record of aggressiveness and success." This move was widely criticized by Israeli politicians as a political maneuver linked to Likud primaries.

Israeli military operations in Gaza continued despite ceasefire discussions. The IDF announced the killing of three terror operatives yesterday: Alaa Imad Khamis Tarams (Army of Islam) and Hassan Ibrahim Shehadeh Qahman (Palestinian Islamic Jihad) in Gaza City, and Ahmad Khudar (Hamas's Jabalia Battalion) in northern Gaza last week. Additionally, Salem Jamal Abd al-Rahman Abu Labad, a Hamas Nukhba Force cell head who infiltrated Kibbutz Nir Oz on October 7, was killed in a strike in southern Gaza. Muhammad Abd al-Nasser Muhammad Khatib, a Hamas Maghazi Battalion commander, was killed in central Gaza on Friday. The IDF justified these strikes by stating the operatives were "advancing attacks on troops" and were "eliminated to remove the threat." Israeli security sources clarified that there is no intention to halt attacks in Gaza as long as Hamas remains armed. The US reportedly expressed surprise and criticism regarding the continuation of targeted killings in Gaza.

In southern Lebanon, the IDF announced the completion of Combat Team 401's 8-month mission, during which over 600 weapons were confiscated and more than 60 Hezbollah operatives were killed. The 401st Armored Brigade has now withdrawn from South Lebanon. An explosion in Kafra, southern Lebanon, lightly injured five Lebanese soldiers. While the Lebanese Armed Forces initially blamed an Israeli strike, they later revised it to a "suspicious object." The IDF asserted it was a bomb planted by Hezbollah, confirming Israeli forces had no presence in Kafra. Israeli drones were also reported to have dropped explosive canisters and incendiary bombs across southern Lebanon, setting fire to lands in al-Tayyiba village, and detonating Lebanese homes in Majdal Zoun.

Amid regional tensions, Israeli security officials expressed frustration with US President Trump's unpredictable decision-making, which "severely undermines operational planning and preparedness," citing two cancelled US operations against Iran within a week. The US has significantly increased its military presence at Ben Gurion Airport, with over 30 tanker aircraft already deployed and 10 more expected, causing severe flight delays. American Airlines announced the cancellation of all flights to Israel until March 27, 2027.

Defense Minister Bezalel Smotrich advocated for the re-establishment of Jewish settlements in Gaza after achieving full control and opposed the formation of a "Peace Council" involving multinational forces. Prime Minister Netanyahu, in a closed-door discussion, stated that a temporary detention law for Haredim had failed and promised a "full conscription law" after the next elections, where those not studying Torah would face conscription or jail. A naval military exercise is scheduled for August 3-4, 2026, in the maritime area between Shavei Tzion and Ashdod.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli military operations in the Gaza Strip resulted in the deaths of several individuals. The IDF confirmed killing Alaa Imad Khamis Tarams (Army of Islam) and Hassan Ibrahim Shehadeh Qahman (Palestinian Islamic Jihad) in Gaza City yesterday, and Ahmad Khudar (Hamas's Jabalia Battalion) in northern Gaza last week. Additionally, Salem Jamal Abd al-Rahman Abu Labad, a Hamas Nukhba Force head involved in the October 7 Nir Oz raid, was killed in southern Gaza, and Muhammad Abd al-Nasser Muhammad Khatib, a Hamas Maghazi Battalion commander, was killed in central Gaza. Palestinian medical sources reported 18 fatalities in Gaza from Israeli attacks this morning, including one in Jabalia, and 8 more Palestinians, including 2 children, were killed despite the ceasefire. Gaza's Health Ministry stated that July 2026 was the deadliest month of the year, with 152 Palestinians killed, including 21 children.

Regarding ceasefire and negotiations, US President Trump claimed a "historic" agreement was reached for the complete disarmament of Hamas and other resistance groups. However, a Hamas official clarified that the proposal only covers "heavy weapons storage" and does not signify abandoning resistance. Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu's spokesperson expressed concern to Reuters about Hamas's disarmament plan, and Israeli security sources affirmed no intention to cease attacks in Gaza until Hamas is disarmed. Nikolay Mladenov, the High Commissioner of the Peace Council for Gaza, condemned Israel (without naming it) for civilian deaths and destruction of medical equipment. Palestinian rescuers recovered the body of an unborn child from its mother's womb after an Israeli attack in Gaza City. Hamas has reportedly begun distributing rifles to its operatives in Gaza under the guise of personal weapons.

In the West Bank, extremist Israeli settlers carried out attacks overnight and on Sunday morning, injuring several Palestinians and damaging homes, vehicles, and infrastructure. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich publicly advocated for the resettlement of Jews in Gaza once full control is established, stating there is "no other solution."

LEBANON
An explosion in the southern Lebanese town of Kafra lightly wounded five Lebanese soldiers. The Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) initially claimed it was an Israeli strike but later retracted, stating the blast was caused by a "suspicious object" and investigations are ongoing. The Israeli military (IDF) clarified that the explosive device did not belong to the IDF and assessed it to be a Hezbollah bomb, noting that Israeli forces have never had a presence in Kafra, which is outside their south Lebanon buffer zone.

Israeli military aggression in southern Lebanon continued, with reports of Israeli drones dropping explosive canisters and incendiary bombs across the region and setting fire to vast areas of al-Tayyiba village. Additionally, Israeli forces were reported to have detonated Lebanese homes in Majdal Zoun.

The IDF announced the completion of Combat Team 401's 8-month mission in southern Lebanon. During this period, the team confiscated over 600 weapons and eliminated more than 60 Hezbollah operatives. The 401st Armored Brigade has now withdrawn from the area.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Attacks against Kurdish-Iranian opposition forces in northern Iraq continued overnight. Saudi media reported that Nechirvan Barzani, President of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, is scheduled to meet Al-Jolani in Damascus tomorrow.

In Iraq, an explosion occurred at the Al-Taji military base north of Baghdad, affecting an ammunition depot belonging to the 9th Armored Division. Iraqi Security Media Cell attributed the incident to high temperatures, and civil defense teams are working to extinguish the fire. The Al-Taji base is used by US coalition forces. The Iraqi government denied reports of US aircraft landing at Ain al-Asad Air Base in Anbar Province. Iraq's National Security Advisor announced an agreement to open a NATO office in Baghdad.

Regarding US military movements, a US Air Force C-130J military transport aircraft was tracked landing in northern or western Iraq after departing from Aqaba, Jordan, remaining for several hours. Additionally, C-17 Globemaster III aircraft activity was reported, with one flying from Osan Air Base (South Korea) to Al Udeid Air Base (Qatar) via Ramstein, potentially carrying air defense interceptors, and several others arriving at Sweihan Air Base in Abu Dhabi. Press TV claimed that Iranian precision drones crippled US Patriot air-defense systems in Erbil, forcing a hasty American pullout.

An accident involving a bus carrying Iranian pilgrims in Wasit, Iraq, resulted in the deaths of several Iranian pilgrims, along with an Iraqi Army colonel and a soldier. Syrian leader Ahmad Al-Shara ordered the deployment and stationing of forces to Syria's borders with Lebanon and Iraq.

GULF STATES
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) reportedly contacted US President Donald Trump on Saturday, expressing concern about Trump's plans for extensive new military strikes against Iran and asking him to de-escalate. CNN and Axios reported MBS's heavy pressure for de-escalation, which was a factor in Trump's decision to cancel the attack.

However, Gulf states are not unified in their approach. The Wall Street Journal reported that some Gulf countries, including the UAE, are pushing Trump for more decisive action against Iran, believing Iran will not compromise without US escalation, potentially including taking control of the Strait of Hormuz or ground operations. These Gulf allies also requested more air defense interceptors from Washington and guarantees of US military protection if hostilities continue.

Foreign Ministers of Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Qatar held discussions regarding efforts to unify positions aimed at regional de-escalation. Oman is actively mediating negotiations with Iran concerning the management of the Strait of Hormuz.

Amid Iranian threats, Kuwaiti pro-government accounts recirculated videos affirming US protection, with the US Embassy in Kuwait also publishing a statement from former President George H.W. Bush pledging to defend Kuwait. US military transport aircraft (C-17) were observed heading towards Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, potentially carrying radar replacements.

OPEC announced that seven member states agreed to reduce oil production by 188,000 barrels per day. The Bahraini Embassy in Damascus, in cooperation with the Golani government in Syria, is reportedly preventing Shiite visitors from Bahrain from entering Syria for religious pilgrimages. Saudi Arabia is accused by a senior Ansarullah official of employing influencers for psychological warfare against Yemen. The Yemeni Parliament criticized Saudi Arabia for portraying itself as a neutral mediator and urged it to pursue peace instead of foreign alliances.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  US President Trump announced the cancellation of a planned military attack on Iran, attributing the decision to an agreed-upon framework that includes the "Immediate, Complete, and Total Opening of the Hormuz Strait, and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat."
2.  Iranian officials, including the Foreign Ministry spokesperson and Fars News Agency, explicitly denied any agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, labeling Trump's claims as "fake news" and asserting the strait remains closed due to US hostile actions.
3.  Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz publicly announced his intention to replace IDF Central Command Chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, a move the IDF Chief of Staff declared was "not coordinated" and that he has "no intention of replacing commanders in key positions during this sensitive period."
4.  The IDF completed an 8-month mission by Combat Team 401 in South Lebanon, confiscating over 600 weapons and eliminating more than 60 Hezbollah operatives, followed by the withdrawal of the 401st Armored Brigade from the area.
5.  Israeli forces continued targeted strikes in Gaza, killing five terror operatives identified as members of Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, and the Army of Islam, including a Hamas Nukhba Force leader who participated in the October 7 attack on Nir Oz.
6.  An explosion in Kafra, southern Lebanon, wounded five Lebanese soldiers; the IDF attributed the incident to a Hezbollah bomb, contradicting initial Lebanese claims of an Israeli strike.
7.  Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) expressed concern to US President Trump regarding plans for extensive attacks on Iran and advocated for de-escalation, according to US and Saudi reports.
8.  Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that negotiations with Oman concerning the management of the Strait of Hormuz are in their "final stages," though the specific terms and confirmation remain contentious.
9.  The US significantly increased its military presence at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, with over 30 tanker aircraft deployed and more expected, contributing to severe flight delays and American Airlines cancelling flights to Israel until March 2027.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high despite President Trump's declared cancellation of an attack on Iran. The stark contradiction between US claims of an agreement and Iranian denials, coupled with the IRGC considering pre-emptive strikes if diplomacy fails, indicates a volatile environment. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with Iran maintaining its closure and ongoing, contentious negotiations with Oman for a new pathway.

In Gaza, continued Israeli "elimination" strikes against terror operatives, even amid ceasefire discussions, risk further destabilization and humanitarian impact, with July 2026 being the deadliest month for Palestinians this year. Lebanon continues to be an active flashpoint, evidenced by Hezbollah's alleged bombing of a Lebanese Army vehicle and ongoing Israeli strikes, despite the withdrawal of the IDF's 401st Brigade.

The unpredictable nature of US decision-making is a significant concern for Israeli security officials, complicating operational planning. Regionally, Gulf states exhibit a divided military posture, with some advocating for US de-escalation while others, like the UAE, push for more decisive action against Iran, increasing the potential for broader regional involvement. Iran has issued clear red lines, warning of a "powerful" response to any US or Israeli hostile actions, particularly if regional states are involved. The internal situation in Iran, with reports of protest leaders arming and economic strains, adds another layer of instability.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture:** President Trump announced the cancellation of a planned attack on Iran, attributing it to an alleged agreement framework on the Strait of Hormuz and nuclear threat. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Iran's regime must change its expansionist behavior, suggesting a strategy of increasing costs for its actions. The US State Department issued a renewed warning to its citizens in the Middle East to exercise increased caution. The US has significantly increased its military footprint in the region, deploying C-17 transport aircraft to various Gulf bases (Al Udeid, Sweihan, Ali Al Salem) and positioning over 30 aerial tanker planes at Ben Gurion Airport in Israel, with more expected.

**Gulf States:** Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) engaged in discussions with President Trump, expressing concern about the potential for extensive attacks on Iran and urging de-escalation. Conversely, some Gulf states, notably the UAE, are reportedly pressing Trump for more decisive military action against Iran, believing that escalation is necessary for Iran to compromise. Gulf allies have requested additional air defense interceptors and guarantees of US military protection. Foreign Ministers from Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Qatar held talks to consolidate positions aimed at reducing regional tensions. Oman continues its diplomatic engagement with Iran regarding the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwaiti state-aligned media and the US Embassy in Kuwait highlighted historical US pledges of defense amidst Iranian threats. OPEC members collectively agreed to a production cut of 188,000 barrels/day.

**EU Members:** Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that the UK and Bulgaria (along with Ukraine) contacted Iran to confirm they would not participate in a war against Iran. A German appeals court acquitted an Instagram user who compared Israeli actions to the Nazi regime, citing freedom of expression.

**Russia:** Ukrainian drones continued to target Russian facilities, striking refineries in Samara, Saratov, and Ufa. Russia also claimed Ukraine attempted to strike the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. The British Navy seized a Russian ship near Pantelleria.

**Turkey:** Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi reportedly discussed the possibility of US attacks with his Turkish counterpart, although no specific statements on Turkey's stance or actions were provided.

**China:** No information provided.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist regarding President Trump's announcement of a cancelled attack on Iran. While Trump claimed an agreement framework involving the opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat, Iranian officials have vehemently denied any such agreement, calling it "fake news." This fundamental disagreement undermines confidence in any diplomatic breakthrough.

Reporting on the Iran-Oman negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz also presents inconsistencies. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stated the talks are in their "final stages," but the IRGC-affiliated Fars News Agency outright denied any agreement on reopening the strait, and Oman is reportedly seeking official confirmation from the IRGC. The details of the alleged "agreement framework" mentioned by Trump remain vague and unverified by independent sources.

Internally in Israel, a clear contradiction exists between Defense Minister Katz's public announcement of replacing the IDF Central Command chief and the IDF Chief of Staff's statement that such a move was "not coordinated" and that no commanders would be replaced during this sensitive period. This indicates deep friction within the Israeli defense establishment.

Several unverified claims and propaganda indicators are present. Press TV claimed that Iranian precision drones crippled US Patriot missile defense systems in Erbil, forcing a US withdrawal, a claim not corroborated elsewhere. Omid Dana, an Iranian opposition channel, exhibits strong bias and uses highly inflammatory language (e.g., celebrating Iranian economic woes, using derogatory terms for religious figures), which diminishes its reliability as a factual source. His posts often advocate for war and the overthrow of the Iranian regime. Conversely, Press TV's framing of US actions as "out of targets, out of strategy" and a sign of "deep US military and political weakness" serves as propaganda aimed at portraying US military ineffectiveness.

Reporting gaps include the precise nature and terms of the "agreement framework" Trump referenced, the full extent of Iranian military readiness and movements, and a comprehensive update on the status of the Gaza ceasefire negotiations beyond general statements and continued Israeli strikes.
